tools.name: search_texts
tools.description:
Search the Vedaword library of Sanskrit scripture by meaning as well as by wording, so a paraphrased question works and a Sanskrit term reaches passages written in another script. This is the first thing to call for any factual question about what the scriptures say.

Start here when you have words:

tools.name: get_verse
tools.description:
Fetch one verse whole: the Sanskrit in Devanāgarī and IAST, the word-by-word breakdown with the meaning each word carries in this passage, the literary translation, the commentary, and optionally the surrounding verses.

Call it after search_texts when you are going to quote, and whenever the user n

tools.name: lookup_sanskrit_term
tools.description:
Look up a Sanskrit word: its spellings across scripts, the meanings it carries in this corpus, how many verses gloss it, and examples of where it occurs.

Built from the word-by-word breakdowns of some 30 000 verses, so these are the meanings translators actually assigned to the word in these texts

tools.name: find_similar_verses
tools.description:
Given a verse, find other passages in the library that say something close to it — by meaning, not by shared words. Start here when you already have a verse; when you only have words, a question or a term, use search_texts.

Use it to check whether a teaching appears elsewhere before presenting it a

tools.name: get_vaishnava_calendar
tools.description:
Ekadashi fasts, festivals and the appearance and disappearance days of the acharyas in the Gaudiya Vaishnava calendar, computed for one place. Call it for any question about when an Ekadashi or a festival falls, or when to break a fast.

tools.name: list_works
tools.description:
List the works with their sizes, shelf, author and available languages. Call it at the start of a conversation about scripture, or when you need work slugs for filtering. The list is short by default: no descriptions.

tools.name: list_authors
tools.description: List the authors the tradition names, grouped by period, each with a short note and the books credited to them. tools.description:

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "search_texts" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Search the Vedaword library of Sanskrit scripture by meaning as well as by wording, so a paraphrased question works and a Sanskrit term reaches passages written…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "get_verse" appears informational but accepts parameters (context) that enable code/file/secret access.
